passage: In PE class, the teacher told Sumit's group to pick teams. Sumit, who wore a hearing aid and sometimes asked people to repeat things, stood at the side. Kabir whispered, "Don't pick him, he's weird." Two others nodded. Mridul's stomach clenched. He didn't want to be the one to argue, and he was afraid they'd turn on him. He looked at Sumit's face and saw him pretend not to notice. Mridul said nothing, but when it was his turn, he quietly said, "Sumit, come on my side." Kabir rolled his eyes. Mridul kept his gaze on the ball. Sumit walked over and gave him a small nod.

qa.q: What did Sumit wear that made him stand out to the group?
Why did Mridul stay quiet when Kabir whispered, "Don't pick him"?
qa.a: He was afraid to disagree and worried the others would turn on him.

qa.q: What could Mridul do next to keep helping Sumit?
qa.a: He can keep being friendly in small ways, like picking him for his side, and later speak to a teacher if the exclusion goes on.

qa.q: How might Sumit be feeling when he pretends not to notice the whispering?
qa.a: Probably hurt and trying to protect himself, which is why he acted as if he had not heard.

grounding: A child afraid to disagree with friends who exclude a different child stays quietly friendly with him.

passage:
I'm Uday. In Class 5, a new boy called Joel joined our section. He hummed while he worked and flapped his hands when he got excited about trains. My friends thought he was weird. Urmila said, "If anyone sits with Joel, they can't sit with us." Everyone agreed. I agreed too, out loud. Inside I felt sick and scared. I didn't want to be alone at lunch.
But Joel knew every train route in the country, and I wanted to hear about them.
So I did small things. I said hi at the gate. I lent him my blue pen. In library period, where Urmila couldn't see, I sat with him, and he showed me a map of the Konkan line.
After a month, Urmila caught us. I waited for trouble. Instead she sat down and asked, "Which is the longest route?"

qa.q: What did Joel show Uday in library period?
qa.a: A map of the Konkan line.

qa.q: Why did Uday agree out loud with Urmila?
qa.a: Uday was scared of being alone at lunch, even though agreeing felt sick inside.

qa.q: What small brave steps did Uday take?
qa.a: Saying hi at the gate, lending the blue pen and sitting with Joel in library period.

qa.q: How might Joel have experienced Uday's small kindnesses?
qa.a: As one friendly face in a class that was shutting him out; he happily shared his train maps.

grounding: A child afraid to disagree with friends who exclude a different boy stays quietly friendly with him, which helps him and takes courage.

passage:
Coach's note, football practice, Thursday
The boys have been leaving Farhan out since he joined; he is new, speaks mostly Kashmiri and Urdu, and is shy. Today when teams were picked, the captain said, "Not him, he doesn't even understand what we say." The others laughed. I saw Tushar look down at his boots, clearly uncomfortable but silent.
Then in the match, Tushar passed to Farhan three times. On the third pass Farhan scored. At water break Tushar sat beside him and taught him the word "shabaash", and Farhan taught him one back.
After practice I asked Tushar how it felt going against the others. "Scary," he said. "But he's good." I have spoken to the whole team about how we treat new players, and I will pair Farhan and Tushar for drills next week.

qa.q: How many times did Tushar pass to Farhan?
How did Tushar feel about going against the others?
qa.a: Scared, as he told the coach, but sure that Farhan was good.

qa.q: What did the coach do after watching?
qa.a: They spoke to the whole team about how to treat new players and paired Farhan and Tushar for drills.

qa.q: How might Farhan have felt when Tushar sat beside him at water break?
qa.a: Welcomed and less alone, happy enough to teach Tushar a word back.

grounding: A coach's note shows a boy afraid to go against teammates who exclude a new player, yet including him quietly, which helps and shows courage.
